Title: Back to the Moment

Verse 1:
I kept your name inside a pocket watch,
Ticking soft behind my ribs.

Every window holds our lips.

Like letters fading off the page,

Back to the heartbeat under our rain.

So I carry you home in my arms of scars.

Verse 2:
I found a train that never leaves the night,
Platform humming with goodbye.
Your shadow leans against the painted line,
As timetables blur and try to lie.
I wear the hours like a borrowed coat,
Too big for what I’ve learned to be,
And every chime that hits the street
Says love is late, but so are we.

Pre-Chorus:
If I could bribe the moon to stall the tide,
I’d buy back August, buy back pride,
And meet you in the place where we never had to hide.

Back to the moment when it all began.
Find you in the doorway, light on your skin,
Say all the words I didn’t say then.
If time would break, I’d break and start again,
Back to the heartbeat under our rain.
But I can’t unwind this sky of spinning stars,
So I carry you home in my arms of scars.

Bridge:
Maybe the future is a country with no map,
We learn its language by what we lack.
I can’t unring the midnight church bell’s toll,
But I can choose the road my feet now hold.
If every wish is just a key without a lock,
I’ll keep the melody and let go of the clock.

Final Chorus:
I can’t turn the hands, but I can turn the page,
Meet you in the dawn beyond the cage.
Find you in the echo, softer than then,
Love you in the world we’re living in.
If time won’t bend, I’ll bend within its frame,
Make room for all the light and all your name.
I won’t unwind this sky of spinning stars,
I’ll learn to live forward with these faithful scars.

Outro:
Let the clock keep talking; I’ll keep walking on,
Where the hours learn to listen, and the heart grows strong.

[Country]=Brazil\n[Genre]=Bossa Nova\n[M:
Here’s a concise breakdown of the Bossa Nova rhythm as heard on Chega de Saudade (Brazil, Bossa Nova), with a focus on the guitar-driven groove that defined the album:

Essentials
- Feel: Relaxed, even 8th-notes with soft, behind-the-beat phrasing
- Meter/tempo: Often notated in 2/4 (or 4/4), moderate tempo; the “swing” comes from syncopation, not from triplets
- Texture: Subtle dynamics, short chord stabs against a steady, understated bass

Guitar “batida” (João Gilberto style)
- Thumb (bass): Alternates root and 5th; think “boom … boom …” steady and soft
- Fingers (chords): Light, syncopated stabs on offbeats (“ands”) with occasional anticipations before chord changes
- A practical 4/4 counting guide (start slow):
  - 1: bass + very light chord together
  - “and” of 1: light chord
  - 2: (often space/ghost), keep the pulse internal
  - “and” of 2: bass (anticipation)
  - 3: bass + light chord
  - “and” of 3: light chord
  - 4: (space)
  - “and” of 4: light chord (often anticipating the next harmony)
- Keep chords short and airy; avoid heavy strums—think gentle taps with immediate release

Drums/Percussion (typical studio approach of the era)
- Kick: Light on 1, occasional anticipations (e.g., “and” of 2)
- Snare/cross-stick: Soft on 2 and 4, never aggressive
- Hats/Ride: Even 8ths, very low volume; brushes or tight hats preferred
- No heavy cymbal wash; the guitar provides most of the groove

Bass (upright or electric emulation)
- Simple root–5th with occasional chromatic approaches
- Locks with the guitar’s thumb, especially on the anticipated “and” of 2 leading into beat 3

Harmony and anticipation
- Chord changes are frequently anticipated by an offbeat stab right before the bar line
- Voice leading stays smooth; extensions are present but played delicately

How to practice the feel
- Step 1: Tap steady 8ths and count “1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &” out loud
- Step 2: Add bass on 1 and (anticipation) “&” of 2, then again on 3
- Step 3: Add short chord stabs on the “&” of 1, “&” of 3, and “&” of 4 (to anticipate changes)
- Step 4: Keep dynamics low; prioritize consistency and evenness over volume

Listening spots on Chega de Saudade
- Chega de Saudade: Archetypal batida—focus on the offbeat chord anticipations
- Desafinado: Even 8ths and understated syncopation; listen for soft cross-stick/snare support
- Bim-Bom: Clear thumb–finger independence on guitar; great for practicing the bass-chord separation

Common pitfalls
- Over-strumming or sustaining chords too long (keep them short and precise)
- Rushing offbeats—let them sit slightly behind the beat
- Overcomplicating the kick/snare; subtlety is key
